mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stabilizes near its current level after a sharp prior rebound, commuting flows stop contracting and retail visits recover modestly within four weeks. The effect is stronger when TRANSIT also stops falling, because the same return-to-routine crowd then reaches shopping areas more easily.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -35.1 at t-3w to around -18.9 at t-0w while TRANSIT stayed depressed around -26.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES holding near current levels and TRANSIT no longer declining.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT below the recent -30% area signals fewer discretionary trips into commercial centers, which reduces retail-and-recreation mobility within one to two weeks. The mechanism fails if transit weakens but retail stays flat because trip substitution shifts to car-based shopping.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30% week-on-week or stays below -30% for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -38.1 at t-3w to -26.1 at t-0w but remains far below baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or remains above the last 4-week mean after TRANSIT crosses below -30% or persists there.

mechanism_narrative: When both GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remain elevated, households consolidate errands locally and make fewer discretionary retail trips. Over four weeks this suppresses RETAIL_REC because essential shopping and home-centered time substitute for recreation-oriented outings.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed positive and RESIDENTIAL stayed above baseline in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both remain above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stops improving and turns down again, it implies a renewed restraint on office attendance that quickly reduces lunch, after-work, and weekday shopping trips. Retail-and-recreation mobility should fall within one week of that reversal.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points from one week to the next and then falls back the following week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved sharply from -35.1 at t-3w to -18.3 at t-1w before easing to -18.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days after a renewed drop in WORKPLACES following a short-lived improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS relative to its recent trough captures substitution toward outdoor leisure during mild conditions, which pulls visits away from malls and indoor recreation venues. Over two to four weeks this lowers RETAIL_REC unless workplace and transit mobility also strengthen.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from its 2-week low and holds that gain for two weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded from -21.7 at t-2w to -10.9 at t-1w before easing to -17.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises despite PARKS holding at or above its recent rebound level for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and TRANSIT stays below baseline together, people remain home-oriented and avoid city-center trips, producing a lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest if neither series moves back toward baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive around 9-14 while TRANSIT remained negative around -26 to -38
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and TRANSIT stays below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A threshold recovery in TRANSIT above -25% signals reopening of regular travel patterns and restores access to shopping districts. Retail mobility should improve within two weeks after that threshold is crossed, but not before.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -25% and remains above that level for at least one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is currently near -26.1, close to the -25% recovery threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 14 days after TRANSIT moves above -25% and holds there.

mechanism_narrative: A joint upturn in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES indicates more out-of-home routine activity and errand chaining, which spills over into discretionary shopping. That combined lift should push RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks, even if PARKS remains volatile.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed slightly positive while WORKPLACES recovered substantially from -35.1 to about -18.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days despite simultaneous strengthening in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES.
